memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: One man from each tribe, each of them the head of his family, is to help you. These are the names of the men who are to assist you: from Reuben, Elizur son of Shedeur; from Simeon, Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai; from Judah, Nahshon son of Amminadab; from Issachar, Nethanel son of Zuar. - Num 1:4-8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God does not ask Moses to do the work alone. He appoints one trusted leader from each tribe to stand alongside him. This is God's pattern all through Scripture — He rarely calls a person to serve in isolation. He surrounds them with others.

These names may look unfamiliar to us, but each man was chosen, named, and given real responsibility. God was building a team. Leadership in God's family has never been about one heroic individual doing everything; it is about many people faithfully carrying their part.

Notice that even Moses — the great leader who spoke with God face to face — needed help. If Moses needed others, so do we. There is no shame in leaning on the people God places around you. In fact, it is God's design.

Look closely and you'll spot Nahshon from the tribe of Judah. Generations later, from that same tribe and family line, Jesus the Messiah would come (Matt 1:2-4). Even in a simple list of helpers, God was quietly weaving His plan of salvation.

Today, thank God for the people who stand beside you — and consider how you might faithfully stand beside someone else.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Who are the people God has placed alongside you to help?
- Are you trying to carry something alone that you were meant to share?
- Whom could you support in their God-given work?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for the people who help me carry life's responsibilities. Teach me to work humbly with others and to be a faithful helper too. Amen.
